review_type: Class2/Class4/UC NI patch follow-up; source read from latest_patch.whl and installed source; no imports or simulations

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 computes compulsory Class 2, which ended in 2024; it adds no voluntary Class 2 abroad, Class 3 residency/contribution-history eligibility, or overseas contribution population. The stated 2026 policy remains not expressible.
corrections.measure: National Insurance: Remove access to Class 2 National Insurance contributions (NICs) and increase the initial residency and contributions history requirements for Class 3 NICs for individuals abroad from 6 April 2026
corrections.missing_machinery: Population is people living abroad paying voluntary Class 2/3 contributions; no contribution records or voluntary-contribution rules (ni_class_3 is an input).
corrections.scope_note: Ends voluntary Class 2 access and tightens Class 3 conditions for individuals abroad (individual contributions).

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 class_2_liable uses the lower profits threshold from 2022-23, so changing SPT does not change compulsory cash liability in the treated-as-paid period. After abolition flat_rate is zero. This revenue-loss costing still needs voluntary-payment/contribution-record channels, which remain absent.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions: impact of maintaining the Lower Earnings Limit and Small Profits Threshold at 2022-23 levels
corrections.missing_machinery: No NI contribution/qualifying-year records or voluntary Class 2/3 payment rules. The compulsory treated-as-paid band is now represented, but preserving the SPT/LEL credit boundary and voluntary payment behaviour is not.
corrections.scope_note: Thresholds governing self-employed and employee NI records.

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 carries GBP 3.45/week from 2023-04-06 and zero compulsory rate from 2024-04-06. class_2_liable retains the lower-profits-threshold test for a reversal: restore the flat rate and pre-abolition Class 4 annual_maximum.includes_class_2 from April 2024. The compulsory household liability leg is expressible; voluntary payments were retained by the policy and remain outside this construction. Full-year self-employment is assumed by ni_class_2.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): abolish Class 2 self-employed NICs liability from April 2024
corrections.scope_note: Class 2 NICs are borne by the self-employed.

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 class_2_liable uses the lower profits threshold from 2022-23, so changing SPT does not change compulsory cash liability in the treated-as-paid period. After abolition flat_rate is zero. This revenue-loss costing still needs voluntary-payment/contribution-record channels, which remain absent.
corrections.measure: NICs: freeze the Lower Earnings Limit and Small Profits Threshold for one year from April 2024
corrections.missing_machinery: No NI contribution/qualifying-year records or voluntary Class 2/3 payment rules. The compulsory treated-as-paid band is now represented, but preserving the SPT/LEL credit boundary and voluntary payment behaviour is not.
corrections.scope_note: Thresholds governing self-employed and employee NI records.

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 explicitly implements the treated-as-paid band: class_2_liable uses relevant ni_class_4_profits above lower_profits_threshold (11908 for 2022-23,12570 from 2023-24), with the lower_profits_threshold_applies switch true from 2022-04-06. Reversal sets that switch false to restore SPT-based compulsory payments; retain SPT as the credit boundary. The flat-rate cash formula uses contribution weeks (52 or 53), not always 52. Later events abolition must be removed from a vintage baseline separately.
corrections.measure: National Insurance: reduce class 2 NICs payments on profits between £6,725 and £12,570
corrections.scope_note: Self-employed with profits between the small profits threshold and lower profits limit stop paying Class 2.

corrections.expressibility_note: Row is zero in every year. The 2.125.1 patch fixes compulsory Class 2 dates and treated-as-paid liability; it adds no voluntary-payment rate/base formula, so this voluntary rate freeze remains not expressible.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): freeze Class 2 and 3 rates for 2024-25
corrections.missing_machinery: Voluntary Class 2 and Class 3 contributions are not modelled: ni_class_3 is an input with no formula, and ni_class_2 computes compulsory full-year payments only, with compulsory flat_rate zero from 2024-04-06.
corrections.scope_note: Income-tax head (zero) of the Class 2/3 rate freeze; household measure.

corrections.expressibility_note: The 2.125.1 patch fixes compulsory Class 2 dates and treated-as-paid liability; it adds no voluntary-payment rate/base formula, so this voluntary rate freeze remains not expressible.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): freeze Class 2 and 3 rates for 2024-25
corrections.missing_machinery: Voluntary Class 2 and Class 3 contributions are not modelled: ni_class_3 is an input with no formula, and ni_class_2 computes compulsory full-year payments only, with compulsory flat_rate zero from 2024-04-06.
corrections.scope_note: Voluntary Class 2 and Class 3 NICs rates paid by individuals.

corrections.expressibility_note: Row is zero in every year. The 2.125.1 patch fixes compulsory Class 2 dates and treated-as-paid liability; it adds no voluntary-payment rate/base formula, so this voluntary rate freeze remains not expressible.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): freeze Class 2 and 3 rates for 2024-25
corrections.missing_machinery: Voluntary Class 2 and Class 3 contributions are not modelled: ni_class_3 is an input with no formula, and ni_class_2 computes compulsory full-year payments only, with compulsory flat_rate zero from 2024-04-06.
corrections.scope_note: Welfare head (zero) of the Class 2/3 rate freeze; household measure.

corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal sets class_2.flat_rate to zero from the scheduled pre-event abolition date; both event-vintage worlds must restore the appropriate compulsory Class 2 path rather than use abolition in 2024 as the baseline. 2.125.1 tests ni_class_4_profits against SPT before 2022 and multiplies the weekly rate by contribution weeks (53 in 2019-20, otherwise 52 in this costing window). The bill provisions not named by the PMD and voluntary-payment legs remain unknown/unrepresented; partial retained.
corrections.measure: NICs: delay NICs Bill by one year and maintain Class 2 NICs
corrections.missing_machinery: Other provisions of the delayed NICs Bill (the PMD text does not list them) and voluntary Class 2/Class 3 contributions have no representation; ni_class_3 is an input.
corrections.scope_note: Keeping Class 2 NICs (instead of abolishing them) is a liability on self-employed individuals.

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 improves compulsory Class 2 cash liability, not the State Pension/contributory-benefit record derived from past contributions. This benefit consequence therefore remains not expressible.
corrections.measure: NICs: delay NICs Bill by one year and maintain Class 2 NICs
corrections.missing_machinery: No NI contribution records or contributory-entitlement tests: contributory ESA/JSA, Maternity Allowance and State Pension are reported amounts or data-driven.
corrections.scope_note: Welfare consequence of the in-scope Class 2 measure: contributions preserve contributory benefit entitlement.

corrections.expressibility_note: Set Class 2 compulsory flat_rate to zero from 2018-04-06 (later withdrawn). 2.125.1 has a cash liability formula and dated pre-abolition weekly rates/SPT values; adjust Class 4 annual_maximum.includes_class_2 where required by the event-vintage abolished-compulsory scenario. The planned contributory-entitlement changes are a separate fiscal concept; voluntary payments and contribution records remain absent.

2.125.1 explicitly implements the treated-as-paid band: class_2_liable uses relevant ni_class_4_profits above lower_profits_threshold (11908 for 2022-23,12570 from 2023-24), with the lower_profits_threshold_applies switch true from 2022-04-06. Reversal sets that switch false to restore SPT-based compulsory payments; retain SPT as the credit boundary. The flat-rate cash formula uses contribution weeks (52 or 53), not always 52. Later events abolition must be removed from a vintage baseline separately. UC deducts actual ni_class_2 in uc_national_insurance_on_earnings, and the self-employed MIF NI formula now uses the same liability helper and contribution-week count on notional floor income.
corrections.measure: National Insurance: reduce Class 2 NICs payments on profits between £6,725 and £12,570
corrections.scope_note: UC knock-on of the Class 2 change (UC deducts Class 2 from self-employed earnings).

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 keys Class 4 LPL 11908 on 2022-04-06 and 12570 on 2023-04-06. Class 1 PT carries the July 2022 step 241.73/week. Reversal restores pre-measure PT 190/week and the pre-measure indexed annual LPL. Class 4 is annual on ni_class_4_profits; Class 1 employee liability is monthly.
corrections.measure: National Insurance: increase annual primary threshold and lower profits limit to £12,570 from July 2022
corrections.scope_note: Raises the Class 1 primary threshold and Class 4 lower profits limit to GBP 12,570.

corrections.expressibility_note: 2.125.1 dates the combined current-law Class 4 main rate 0.06 at 2024-04-06. A current-law marginal reversal of the AS 2023 one-point cut sets 0.07. A vintage-faithful AS 2023 pair instead uses 0.09 before and 0.08 after, excluding the later SB 2024 two-point cut. ni_class_4 and its annual-maximum formula read this rate.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 1p cut to the main rate of Class 4 self-employed NICs from April 2024
corrections.scope_note: Class 4 NICs are borne by the self-employed.

corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal restores Class 4 main rate 0.08 from 2024-04-06 against 0.06 after SB 2024. 2.125.1 keys 0.09 from 2023-04-06 and 0.06 from 2024-04-06 (both AS 2023 and SB 2024 cuts), and ni_class_4/ni_class_4_main read that rate on ni_class_4_profits.
corrections.measure: National Insurance contributions (NICs): 2 percentage point cut to the main rate of Class 4 self-employed NICs from 6 April 2024
corrections.scope_note: Class 4 NICs on self-employment profits; legal incidence on the self-employed.

corrections.expressibility_note: The event-vintage 2022-23 NICs increase is +1.25 pp on Class 1 employee main/additional, employer and Class 4 main/additional rates. 2.125.1 current law instead carries the later-repeal blended Class 4 annual rates 9.73%/2.73% from 2022-04-06 and 9%/2% from 2023-04-06; a faithful AB 2021 world must explicitly use 10.25%/3.25% for 2022-23. Class 1 employee rates are monthly; its additional-rate YAML still has the separate late-reversion date gap. The levy after 2023 is a separate head/gap.
corrections.measure: Health and Social Care Levy introduced from April 2022: gross yield
corrections.scope_note: 1.25pp rise in Class 1 employee, employer and Class 4 NICs in 2022-23 (the levy's first year).

corrections.expressibility_note: Reversal restores pre-repeal Class 1 rates from 2022-11-06, and Class 4 annual 2022-23 rates 10.25%/3.25%. 2.125.1 post-repeal Class 4 annual rates are 9.73%/2.73% from 2022-04-06, returning 9%/2% from 2023-04-06. Class 1 employee rates are monthly, while its additional-rate YAML still reverts only 2024-04-04 and needs explicit vintage values. The later-year small NICs tails are indirect effects.
corrections.measure: National Insurance: reverse temporary 1.25pp increase in NICs rates from November 2022, and cancel the Health and Social Care Levy
corrections.scope_note: Reversal of the 1.25pp NICs rate rise from 6 November 2022 (employee, employer and Class 4); liability on earners and employers per employee.
